topics.title: The Chicken Problem
topics.text: Yes, I know that there are a lot of threads about this but because they’re so old I can’t find any. 100 chickens sit peacefully in a circle. They suddenly poke the chicken to the right or to the left of them. What is the expected value of unpecked chickens? Can you prove this is $25$ is an Algebraic way? Here’s my explanation. There is a $\frac{1}{4}$ chance that the chicken will be pecked by the chicken to the left. There is a $\frac{1}{4}$ chance that the chicken will be pecked by the chicken to the right. There is a $\frac{1}{4}$ chance that the chicken will be pecked by both chickens. Leaving a $\frac{1}{4}$ chance that the chicken won’t be pecked. So $1$ out of $4$ chickens will not be pecked. This means the expected value of chickens to be unpecked is $25$. Is this solution valid and if not can I have an Algebraic Solution as I said above.

topics.title: Math Team Contest December 2017
topics.text:
500th Post

Test is out now!!! Teams are formed in order of signups, with one team of 4. You can still sign up, but you'll have to be a one man team until more people sign up. You may make PMs now.

You may have remembered me from my first Math Team Contest, held in October. Well, here is my second one. Rules are slightly different.



Rules

1. Sign up in the standard signups format, with Signups (X)1.USERNAME 1

2. USERNAME 2

3. USERNAME 3

......
, where X is the number of people. Teams of 5 are formed in the order of signups.

2. Problems are to be worked on in your teams. You may talk with each other in a PM (you don't have to include me in it) about the problems. You submit one response per team in a separate PM.

3. There are 7 questions total. No tiebreakers are in this contest, as we couldn't agree on a good time for last time's tiebreakers.

4. Test will be released on December 24, 2017. Submissions are due January 7, 2018. If that does not work out, please let me know and I may change it.



Difficulty

Some are MathCounts school round level, others chapters or state level.



Have fun and enjoy!



Some info: http://artofproblemsolving.com/community/c3h1556496p9638229



EDIT: A mistake was fixed on #1. The new test is out now. Thanks to deew for pointing that out!



Next MTC is in August/September 2018

topics.title: A random problem I made
topics.text:
In the small town of Disasterland, there is a 20% chance that there will be an earthquake in any given year. If an earthquake occurs in any given year there is a 75% chance that a tsunami will occur in that same year, and if an earthquake doesn't occur in any given year there is a 40% chance that a tsunami will occur in that same year. Given that there has been  a tsunami in the year 2019, what is the probability there was an earthquake?



SolutionDenominator = $0.15 + 0.32$

Numerator = 0.15. Therefore the answer is $\frac{15}{47}$
